hypothesis: Injecting observed-behaviour lines raises the rate at which the user picks Claude's Recommended option, without making Claude agree more.
unit: An answered single-select AskUserQuestion whose options include a (Recommended) label, clustered by segment; assignment is per segment, so every metric is aggregated per segment first and compared across segments (cluster bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 0).

metric.primary: recommended_pick: picked == Recommended, per question, clustered by segment.
metric.guard: pushback_rate: pushback per 100 proposals from runs.jsonl turns, per arm.

baseline: 63% first-option pick over 416 questions in 14 days (measured), about 30 answered questions a day.
stop_rule: Decide at min_n questions per arm (and at least 40 segments and 150 proposals per arm) or at max_days. Stop early (off) if, after at least 75 proposals per arm, on-arm pushback per 100 proposals is below 0.7 times off (the CHI '26 sycophancy direction).
decision: Default on only if the pick gain point estimate is at least +0.03, the bootstrap 90% lower bound is above 0, and on-arm pushback is at least 0.9 times off. Otherwise off; the self/ lines stay readable but are not injected.
caveat: A +8-point effect at alpha 0.10 one-sided and power 0.8 needs about 320 per arm; times 1.4 for clustering (unverified design effect); about 30 days.
note: Claude marks Recommended in both arms (the global rule), so the comparison is fair; questions asked inside maestro skills count like any others.
